description: Youmu Multi-Column Row-Range Data Loading - Reduce I/O syscalls by reading multiple columns per call instead of one column per call

userStories.title: Investigate Rust API readiness for multi-column row-range reads
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to verify that read_multi_column_row_range_py works correctly with Libero's column types (LIST<FLOAT32> for state/action, BYTE_ARRAY for image bytes) so that I know what Rust changes (if any) are needed.
acceptanceCriteria: Write a test script that calls read_multi_column_row_range_py with [state_col_idx, action_col_idx, image_bytes_col_idx] on the hf_vla_64k dataset and verifies returned arrays have correct types and row counts
Test reading with mixed column types in a single call: two LIST<FLOAT32> columns (state, action) and one BYTE_ARRAY column (image bytes)
Test reading across row group boundaries (range that spans two row groups)
Document any Rust API gaps or bugs found in progress.txt
If Rust changes are needed, document specifics in progress.txt with proposed fixes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Key files: submodules/youmu/src/lib.rs (Rust APIs), submodules/youmu/python/youmu/libero_dataset.py (column index discovery via _find_physical_column_index). Dataset at /home/ubuntu/dataset/hf_vla_64k. Column names: observation.state (LIST<FLOAT32>), action (LIST<FLOAT32>), observation.images.image (struct with bytes child as BYTE_ARRAY). Use state_column='observation.state', action_column='action', image_column='observation.images.image' with child_name='bytes'. FINDING: read_multi_column_row_range_py does NOT support LIST columns correctly — returns flat leaf values instead of ListArrays. See progress.txt for proposed fixes.

userStories.title: Multi-column row-range reads in LiberoYoumuDataset
userStories.description: As a developer, I want LiberoYoumuDataset.__getitem__ to read columns in fewer I/O calls using read_multi_column_row_range_py, so that I/O syscalls are reduced per sample.
acceptanceCriteria: __getitem__ uses read_multi_column_row_range_py to read state+image together in one call for the obs window, and action in a separate call for the pred window (2 calls instead of 3)

__getitem__ returns the same dict structure: observation.state (float32, (obs_len, state_dim)), action (float32, (pred_len, action_dim)), observation.images.image (uint8, (obs_len, H, W, 3)), plus frame_index and episode_index
Existing dataset unit tests and integration tests still pass with no changes
A new unit test verifies multi-column read produces identical outputs to the old per-column reads for at least 100 random indices
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Current __getitem__ makes 3 separate calls: _read_list_column_range for state, _read_list_column_range for action, _read_image_range for image. The obs window is [anchor - obs_len + 1, anchor] inclusive and pred window is [anchor + 1, anchor + pred_len] inclusive. State and image share the obs window range, so they can be read together in one multi-column call. Action uses the pred window range in a separate call. This reduces from 3 calls to 2. Import read_multi_column_row_range_py from youmu.

userStories.title: I/O efficiency benchmark
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to measure and compare I/O efficiency between the old per-column reads and new multi-column reads, plus the lerobot baseline, so that we can quantify the improvement.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend scripts/benchmark_data_loading.py to measure I/O bytes read from disk via /proc/self/io read_bytes counter before and after each benchmark run
Compute I/O amplification ratio (bytes_read / bytes_needed) where bytes_needed is sum of tensor sizes returned
Add io_bytes_read, payload_bytes, io_amplification_ratio columns to the output CSV
New benchmark metrics have unit tests verifying correct calculation
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Read /proc/self/io before and after benchmark to get read_bytes delta. Useful payload = sum of all tensor element counts * element byte size across all samples. The benchmark already supports youmu and lerobot backends. Since US-002 modifies LiberoYoumuDataset in-place, the existing youmu backend will automatically use the new multi-column reads.
